text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury suggests a likely tendon or ligament injury, such as a mallet finger or a fracture. Do you have difficulty straightening the tip of the finger, and is there any visible deformity at the end joint?

text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Finger_X-Ray

The inability to flex the DIP joint with an extended resting position and pain at that joint following trauma is highly suggestive of a flexor tendon injury, specifically a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion (Jersey finger), so I need to rule out a bony avulsion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray_of_the_Right_Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the X-ray rules out fracture but confirms soft tissue swelling, and your symptoms point to a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion (Jersey finger), I have enough information. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
